column1: # OWASP ZAP scan rules tuning
# Format: rule-id<TAB>threshold<TAB>description
# Valid thresholds (zap-baseline only): IGNORE | INFO | WARN | FAIL
#   (PASS is also accepted). LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH are NOT valid here — using them
#   makes zap-baseline fail to load this file and abort with exit code 3.
# Rule IDs and their OWASP Top 10 tags: https://www.zaproxy.org/alerttags/
# Threshold semantics: IGNORE suppresses the alert, INFO/WARN report it without
# failing, and FAIL makes the scan fail on that alert. Start conservative —
# tighten (move rules to FAIL) as findings are triaged.
# NOTE: zap-baseline requires 3 tab-separated tokens per line (id, threshold,
# description). Lines with only 2 tokens abort the scan with exit code 3.
# Weekly triage loop and justification standards:
# docs/security/zap-triage-runbook.md
# Timestamp disclosure (often build hashes, not real timestamps)

column3: Timing disclosure false positive: hits are build/deploy metadata timestamps, not sensitive data (tuned during baseline triage)

column3: Private IP disclosure: scans target localhost/CI-internal addresses, so hits are a scan-target artifact, not an app property
